title: Separability Is the Absence of a Repeated Linear Factor, in Every Characteristic
description: Answers the parent's open question relating the Hasse multiplicity factor theorem to separability. Mathlib defines a polynomial as separable iff it is coprime to its ordinary derivative. Reusing the parent's characteristic-free double-root criterion (X − a)² ∣ p ↔ p(a) = 0 ∧ p′(a) = 0, this entry makes the link to repeated roots explicit and computable: a separable polynomial over any nontrivial commutative ring has no repeated linear factor (¬ (X − a)² ∣ p for all a), and over a field a nonzero polynomial that splits is separable iff it has no repeated linear factor (separable ↔ ∀ a, ¬ (X − a)² ∣ p). Two explicit characteristic-2 witnesses (X² + X separable, X² inseparable) show the ordinary-derivative criterion behaves correctly even where the parent's hasseDeriv_detects_char_p flags the ordinary derivative as blind at higher multiplicity. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: the Hasse multiplicity factor theorem in all characteristics. This entry answers its open question linking the criterion to separability, using the parent's characteristic-free double_root_iff as the repeated-root bridge.

overview.historicalContext: A polynomial over a field is called separable when it has no repeated roots in an algebraic closure — equivalently, when it shares no common factor with its derivative. Classically (Dummit–Foote §13.5) this is detected by the derivative test: a is a repeated root of p iff p(a) = 0 and p′(a) = 0, so p is separable iff gcd(p, p′) = 1. The parent entry recasts the underlying repeated-root criterion in a characteristic-free way using Hasse derivatives, proving (X − a)² ∣ p ↔ p(a) = 0 ∧ p′(a) = 0 over an arbitrary commutative ring with no p ≠ 0 hypothesis. This leaf carries that bridge across to Mathlib's notion of separability (coprimality with the ordinary derivative) and records the explicit consequence: separability is exactly the absence of a repeated linear factor (X − a)².
overview.problemStatement: Relate the parent's multiplicity factor theorem to separability. Show that a separable polynomial has no repeated linear factor in every characteristic, and that over a field a nonzero polynomial which splits is separable iff no (X − a)² divides it. Exhibit explicit characteristic-2 witnesses confirming the ordinary-derivative-based separability criterion remains correct where the parent showed the ordinary derivative to be blind at higher multiplicity.
overview.proofStrategy: The repeated-root criterion sq_dvd_iff_eval_derivative is the parent's double_root_iff, valid in any commutative ring. From it, Separable.not_sq_dvd follows: if (X − a)² ∣ p then X − a divides both p and p′ (factor theorem), so coprimality of p and p′ (the definition of Separable) forces X − a to be a unit via IsCoprime.isUnit_of_dvd', contradicting not_isUnit_X_sub_C. Over a field, sq_dvd_iff_one_lt_rootMultiplicity identifies (X − a)² ∣ p with a being a multiple root by rewriting through Mathlib's one_lt_rootMultiplicity_iff_isRoot; roots_nodup_iff_forall_not_sq_dvd then turns Multiset.nodup_iff_count_le_one and count_roots into the statement that distinct roots means no repeated linear factor. Composing with Mathlib's nodup_roots_iff_of_splits gives the headline separable_iff_forall_not_sq_dvd. The characteristic-2 witnesses compute the ordinary derivative directly: derivative (X² + X) = C 2 · X + 1 = 1 since 2 = 0 in ZMod 2 (so X² + X is coprime to 1, hence separable), while derivative (X²) = C 2 · X = 0 (so X² is coprime to 0 only if it is a unit, which it is not).
keyInsights: Separability is a multiplicity-≤-1 condition: it only ever needs to detect double roots, and double roots are detected by the ordinary derivative in every characteristic (the m = 1 Hasse derivative equals the ordinary derivative). The divided-power correction the parent needs is only for multiplicities ≥ p.

The bridge from the parent's divisibility form to separability is coprimality: a common divisor of p and p′ must be a unit, so the linear factor X − a can never divide both — this is exactly why no (X − a)² divides a separable polynomial.

The explicit (X − a)²-divisibility characterization separable ↔ ∀ a, ¬ (X − a)² ∣ p is the elementary statement a student expects; Mathlib proves the equivalent facts but phrases them via roots.Nodup or Squarefree, so the divisibility form is assembled here.
The splitting hypothesis is what makes the converse work: only when p splits over F are all of its repeated roots realised by linear factors (X − a)² over F itself, so testing those factors suffices.

Characteristic 2 is the sharp test case: derivative (X²) = 0 makes X² inseparable (coprime to 0 means unit), while derivative (X² + X) = 1 makes X² + X separable — both verdicts correct, confirming the ordinary-derivative criterion despite the parent's char-p warning about higher multiplicities.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 154 lines and 7 theorems linking the parent's Hasse multiplicity factor theorem to separability. The forward direction — separable polynomials have no repeated linear factor — holds over any nontrivial commutative ring in every characteristic, derived from the parent's characteristic-free double_root_iff via coprimality. Over a field, the entry gives the explicit elementary criterion separable ↔ ∀ a, ¬ (X − a)² ∣ p for nonzero split polynomials, and confirms it with characteristic-2 witnesses (X² + X separable, X² inseparable).
conclusion.implications: This answers the parent's open question on relating its multiplicity criterion to separability. It also clarifies why Mathlib defines separability through the ordinary derivative even in positive characteristic: squarefreeness only ever requires detecting double roots, which the ordinary derivative does in every characteristic. The divided-power Hasse correction that the parent introduces is needed only at multiplicities ≥ p, not for the squarefreeness test that underlies separability.
openQuestions: Characterize inseparable irreducibles over a field of characteristic p as the polynomials in Xᵖ (those whose ordinary derivative vanishes identically), and relate this to the vanishing of all Hasse derivatives up to order p − 1.
Formalize the gcd form of the criterion: over a field, p is separable iff gcd(p, p′) is a unit, and extract the squarefree part p / gcd(p, p′).
